week.worked: Monday night at Craven Cottage did most of the work: João Pedro eleven and Rogers eight, nineteen points from two Chelsea picks in a 3-2 he had been waiting a week for. Calafiori added nine at £5.5m. Fifty points and fifth of eleven is a fair week that arrived four days late.
week.didnt: The expensive half of the team again. The armband on a £15.5m striker, plus a £12.0m midfielder and Mbeumo and Shaw alongside him — four picks costing £40m, seven points between them, nine once the armband was counted. Kerkez played ninety minutes at Newcastle and returned nothing.
week.next: Nothing to buy before Friday. The one Chelsea player who beat both of his is Palmer, at £9.5m, and that is a squad question rather than a transfer — the money is currently sitting in Manchester United shirts, and that decision belongs to GW4 at Old Trafford.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Thirteen points, an assist inside thirty seconds and Chelsea's penalties, and he already owns the two Chelsea players either side of him. This is the pick the squad was built to afford and does not contain.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City's left-back at the same £5.5m as Kerkez. Two starts in a row and the seat is real; one is still one.

week.worked: The cheap end held up: Ajer eight at £4.5m and Schade three from a Brentford pair nobody else in the room owns, Szoboszlai eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven. Forty-nine points from a squad whose every worthwhile return came from £7.5m or less.
week.didnt: He put the armband on a Manchester United midfielder and the gloves on a Manchester United goalkeeper on the day United lost 2-0 at Hull: four from the captain, one from Lammens, two from Mbeumo. Ballard blanked, and eight points sat on the bench behind them.
week.next: He is a point behind Xabi and fifteen behind Le Professeur, which is nothing. The exposure to fix is not the number of United players but the goalkeeper on top of them — United have Ipswich at home next, which is the fixture that either settles the question or makes it urgent.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A third Brentford asset at £5.5m, and the one with the highest ceiling of the three. The case is the defensive-contribution rate repeating, not the fourteen on debut.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He owns an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Eleven points at £6.5m is the cheapest way to fix that, and the room has now gone a full gameweek without anybody doing it.

week.worked: The best mid-price spine of the five: Ndiaye nine, Szoboszlai eight, Rogers eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven — forty-five of his fifty-eight from five players priced between £5.5m and £7.5m. Third in the league, second of the five, and no chip spent.
week.didnt: Twelve points on the bench, nine of them Gvardiol, who started at left-back for City while Hume and Shaw kept their places in the eleven. That is the largest bench score in the room and the difference between second and first in it.
week.next: The squad is right and the order is not. Nothing needs buying; the bench needs reading, and it needed reading on Sunday afternoon rather than on Monday night.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: The only Arsenal asset he owns is a defender. At £6.5m the midfielder is the same money as E.Le Fée, who has produced no shots and no chances created.

watchlist.name: De Cuyper
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £4.5m, the highest-scoring defender of the weekend, and Brighton go to Chelsea next. A haul in a 4-0 is a match, not a seat — wait for the second one.

week.worked: Two Arsenal picks nobody else in the room has — Havertz and Mosquera — returned twelve, Tzolis added six, Verbruggen kept a clean sheet at £4.5m and João Pedro brought eleven. Five players costing £31.5m between them made thirty-five of his forty-four.
week.didnt: Two of his eleven never appeared on a pitch. Palestra was left out of Chelsea's matchday squad entirely with what Alonso called a setback, and Aït-Nouri was a substitute at the Etihad while Gvardiol played left-back. Semenyo, his second most expensive outfielder at £8.5m, returned two. Forty-four points is last of the five.
week.next: The gap to fourth is five points, which is one line-up sheet. Both dead slots are cheap defenders, which is the cheapest kind of mistake to fix — but the fix is reading team news on Friday, not spending a transfer on Tuesday.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He owns two Chelsea defenders who did not play and no Chelsea attacker. Thirteen points and the penalties at £9.5m is where that money should have been.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: The player who kept his own pick out of the side, for exactly the same money. If the City defensive slot is worth a place, this is the one that starts.

week.worked: Sixty-four points, top of the five and second in the league, six behind the leader. The starting eleven made fifty-eight of that on its own, and forty-five of the fifty-eight came from Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, Calafiori and João Pedro — five mid-price players rather than one lucky captain, which is the most repeatable week anybody had.
week.didnt: The Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six — two apiece from Kinsky, Diop and Groß, and nothing from Konsa. Cash cost him a point in a 4-0 defeat at Brighton in which Villa conceded four inside thirty-one minutes and had a debutant sent off.
week.next: He leads on squad, not on chip, and that is the version worth having. Two things to watch: whether the lead survives the first week someone else has a chip and he does not, and whether Cash is startable at all with Villa's dressing room where it currently is.

watchlist.name: Ajer
watchlist.note: Eight points at exactly Cash's price, in a side that beat Spurs 3-0. The straight swap if Villa's week gets any worse.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A first half played one chip short wants cheap ceiling rather than cheap safety. This is the shape of that, if the defensive contributions hold up.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: The single biggest collective miss of the opening weekend. Thirteen points, Chelsea's penalties, an assist after thirty seconds and a goal, at 11.7% ownership — and not one of the five owns him, while all five owned the captain who returned two.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Eleven points at £6.5m. Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the midfielder. This was written a gameweek ago and is still true, which makes it a decision now.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City's left-back. Two of the five own a £5.5m City defender who was not in the side and one has the right one on the bench, which is a strange way for a room to be exposed to the same club.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: Hit the defensive-contribution threshold on debut despite coming off early, plus two assists and maximum bonus. The rate is the case; one of the assists was a parried shot that fell to a teammate.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: Twelve points at £7.0m and under 5% owned, which would be the buy of the week if Tottenham had not been working on a deal for a while and Manchester City had not joined on Monday. Nothing to do until 2 September.

watchlist.name: Woltemade
watchlist.note: Newcastle's penalty taker in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker, and a substitute at St James' Park with Osula leading the line and Wissa behind him. The fixtures are still right; the seat is not his.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: An assist inside thirty seconds, the third goal, thirteen points and Chelsea's penalties — the best midfield return of the weekend, owned by none of the five.
verdicts.trigger: The calf flag turning into a missed weekend, or two games spent wide rather than at ten.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Eleven points and Chelsea's fastest goal in a decade, owned by all five and 65% of the game — for once the crowded side of the trade was the right one.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box, and 65% becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Tapped in on debut after a club-record move and got the full ninety Alonso had warned the late World Cup returnees might not get.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide or on the bench once Caicedo and Enzo are back in the Chelsea midfield.

verdicts.name: Sánchez
verdicts.why: Rated three by BBC Sport at Craven Cottage — an early kicking error, beaten at his near post, and a parry turned in for Fulham's second.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or Chelsea signing a goalkeeper before the window shuts.

verdicts.name: Palestra
verdicts.why: Named in a starting eleven in this league and left out of Chelsea's matchday squad altogether; Alonso said he had a setback during the week.
verdicts.trigger: One competitive start. Until then a £5.5m defender with no debut is a slot rather than a player.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: On the bench for the opener, heavily linked with Manchester City, with open questions about his condition after an extended post-World Cup break.
verdicts.trigger: A start in central midfield once the window has shut.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: Six points at £6.0m from a back line that conceded twice, so the return came from somewhere other than a clean sheet.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Brighton, or a second week of attacking returns, before the price is worth paying.

verdicts.name: Gonzalo
verdicts.why: Scored on his Fulham debut, has the penalties, and costs £6.0m at 2.5% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Muniz or Kusi-Asare starting ahead of him once Fulham's forwards are all available.

verdicts.name: King
verdicts.why: Nineteen, Fulham's best player on the night by a distance, the near-post equaliser and a shot from range that nearly made it 3-3, at £5.5m and 0.3% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without ninety minutes. A teenager's breakout night is a night.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two points, ninety minutes, the penalties, and the armband from three of the five — a blank that separated nobody, because the other two captained a midfielder who also returned two.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through the wide players and past him.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: United had twenty-one shots at Hull and sixteen of them were worth under 0.1 expected goals each; the volume runs through him and the quality does not.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Ipswich with the same shot profile, and £12.0m stops being a price and starts being a hole.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, and the Hull post-mortem points at shot quality rather than at the two set plays — which is the slower problem, not the quicker one.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking at home to Ipswich, which makes the GW4 sale automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: A £4.5m defender in a back line that lost 2-0 to a promoted side and conceded two headed set plays.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three restores him; another set-piece collapse and the cheap seat is not worth the slot.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost at Hull to two headers.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit.

verdicts.name: Šeško
verdicts.why: Zero pre-season minutes became twenty-three at Hull, and the start still has not come.
verdicts.trigger: A start plus a goal and he re-enters as a watch — not before.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, owned by four of the five and by 41% of the game — still the closest thing to a free lunch on the list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.5m and a week later still nobody in the room owns him, which has stopped being an oversight and become a choice.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or Arsenal's returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal's penalties at £9.5m, with barely 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation through the Champions League weeks.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m and 6.7% ownership, in a forward line that has not yet settled around Gyökeres.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks as a substitute once Arsenal's attack is fully fit.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real, the seat is borrowed.
verdicts.trigger: Saliba's back clearing. When it does, this pick ends.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six points and a debut that got noticed; a quarter of the game is on him now and the price has not moved.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Central midfield at Newcastle, on Liverpool's penalties, at £7.0m — and 43% of the game is already there, so there is no differential left in it.
verdicts.trigger: A shift back to right-back and the appeal halves.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Twelve points at £7.0m and under 5% owned, with Tottenham working on a deal and Manchester City entering on Monday.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting with him still at Liverpool and still starting.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes at left-back at Newcastle with Frimpong opposite him; a nought in a 2-2 is a scoreline, not a demotion.
verdicts.trigger: One week on the bench, or Liverpool moving to a back three, and £5.5m stops making sense.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back and returned nine — the City defensive seat that actually exists at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: O'Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: A substitute at the Etihad with Gvardiol at left-back, and still in a starting eleven in this league.
verdicts.trigger: One start ahead of Gvardiol. Same price, same club, and only one of them plays.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Ten points on his first City start, in a back line reshuffled around Doku's injury rather than by design.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the XI with Dias and Khusanov fit and £6.0m is wrong.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Eight points from the bench. The trigger set two weeks ago was a start, and he has not had one.
verdicts.trigger: A start while Doku is out. Another cameo, however productive, is not a seat.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Two points at £8.5m from a starting City wide player — the price assumes returns the role has not produced.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks with Cherki and Marmoush getting minutes and this is a sack.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate rather than the two assists, one of which was a parried shot.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the threshold and he is the £5.5m midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Eight points at £4.5m in a Brentford side whose press left Spurs unable to register a shot on target until 3-0 down.
verdicts.trigger: Collins or Kayode taking the aerial returns instead, or one rotation.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: A game-high five second-half shots and a penalty won in a 3-0 — the underlying numbers are ahead of the three points.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks of shot volume without a return and the finishing becomes the story.

verdicts.name: Thiago
verdicts.why: Missed from the spot after converting ten of his previous eleven, blanked in a 3-0 win, and Brentford's run turns hard from GW5.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties to anyone, and £8.0m is a sack the same day.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or a striker arriving before the window shuts.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Nine points on Everton's penalties at £6.0m in a side that opened with a clean sheet; two of the five have him.
verdicts.trigger: Everton's fixtures turning, or the penalty duty moving.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes and the opener in a 2-0 from a £6.5m central midfielder in a side keeping clean sheets.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Spurs did not have a shot on target until 3-0 down, and De Zerbi said afterwards that they are not a team yet.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players back, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Minus one in a 4-0 in which Villa conceded four inside thirty-one minutes and lost a debutant to a red card, with Arsenal at Villa Park next.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or the window closing with Watkins still there and the dressing room settled.

verdicts.name: Watkins
verdicts.why: Training on his own, four Al-Hilal bids rejected, and a manager who answered the question about his absence with silence.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting with him at Villa and back in the starting eleven.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created at £6.0m.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Emersonn
verdicts.why: Nine points and the best xGI of any Ipswich player at £5.5m — a genuinely cheap forward with a role.
verdicts.trigger: One start on the bench once Ipswich's attacking signings settle.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: Newcastle's £6.0m penalty taker in front of the best six-game run on the ticker, and a substitute in the one game so far.
verdicts.trigger: One start. The fixtures have been the case for two weeks and the team sheet still is not.

signals.text: Left out of Chelsea's matchday squad for the opener along with Caicedo. Alonso, pre-match: "During the week they had setbacks. With Moi, we don't want to take risks. They were not ready to play tonight. We go week-by-week, but they were not ready for tonight." Both were at Craven Cottage watching; Gusto started at right wing-back in Palestra's place.
signals.action: a summer signing with no competitive debut and a setback is not a slot worth holding — wait for a team sheet, not a flag

signals.text: A surprise exclusion from the squad at Fulham after a setback in the week; Reece James and Lavia were paired in midfield instead. Alonso said the club will go week-by-week with him.
signals.action: read the Brighton team sheet rather than the 75% flag — there is no return date attached to this one

signals.text: Named on the bench for the opener while heavily linked with Manchester City, with questions raised about his fitness after an extended holiday following the World Cup.
signals.action: a £7.0m midfielder who did not start his club's first league game during a transfer window is a hold at best

signals.text: Rated 3 by BBC Sport at Craven Cottage: an early kicking error, beaten at his near post by Josh King, then a parry into the danger area that Gonzalo García turned in. Alonso spoke only about collective responsibility; Carragher said Chelsea "will never win the league" with him in goal.
signals.action: Chelsea's six-game run is kind, but the £5.0m route into it is the wrong end of the pitch

signals.text: Training away from Alonso's first team and left out at Fulham, with Nottingham Forest in advanced talks a year and £30m after Chelsea signed him from Ipswich.
signals.action: the consequence is at Forest, not Chelsea — a Delap arrival puts real pressure on Wood and Igor Jesus rather than backing them up

signals.text: Four Al-Hilal offers rejected, the latest close to £40m and still short of Villa's valuation. He returned from an extended break after the World Cup, has been training on his own, and has made his feelings clear to the hierarchy. Emery, asked why he was not in the squad at Brighton: "This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence."
signals.action: an £8.0m forward who is not being selected. Nothing to own here until the deadline passes on 1 September

signals.text: Newcastle's confirmed XI at St James' Park had Osula leading the line and Wissa behind him, with Woltemade on the bench.
signals.action: hold off — the penalty taker in front of the best six-game run on the ticker is not currently starting

signals.text: Four goals conceded inside thirty-one minutes at Brighton, a debutant sent off, the club's all-time record Premier League goalscorer left out of the squad and training alone, and a manager answering questions about him with silence. Arsenal at Villa Park is next.
signals.action: no Villa asset is safe to start in GW2, and that includes the cheap defenders — the problem is not the fixture

signals.text: Four debutants started at Brentford and an £85m signing came off the bench in a 3-0 defeat, with no shot on target until 3-0 down. De Zerbi: "I think we are not a team yet, for a lot of reasons." He put it down to a disrupted pre-season and a side that could not live with Brentford's press.
signals.action: target Spurs rather than own them until the window shuts and the fixtures soften around GW7

signals.text: The post-mortem on the 2-0 at Hull puts the problem somewhere other than the set pieces: twenty-one shots, sixteen of them worth under 0.1 expected goals apiece — the same pattern as last season, when United had the third-worst average open-play shot quality of any top-half club. Opta had rated them 68.9% to win before kick-off.
signals.source: Andrew Beasley, via the touchline digest of 2026-08-25
signals.action: this is the slower problem, not the quicker one. Set-piece goals stop; bad shots do not. Ipswich at home is the test

signals.text: Thirty-nine senior players remain on the books with a week to sell or loan. Mudryk, Nicolas Jackson, Essugo and Marc Guiu were all left out of the squad entirely for the opener.
signals.action: Chelsea's team sheets are being written by the window as much as by form until 1 September

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week, not against the table. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used — and the manager who played it still leads, which is the point: the chip was not the reason.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Gameweek 1 finished with two players in one squad in this league who were never in their club's matchday eleven, and three of the weekend's best mid-price returns coming from players who started on a bench or out of position.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

roast.text: Mr CR7 finishes Gameweek 1 third in the league and second of the five, six points behind Le Professeur, having left twelve points on his bench — nine of them a Manchester City left-back who started, while a £4.5m defender playing out of position on the right wing kept his place in the eleven. He did not get a single decision about which players to own wrong. He got one decision about which of them to look at wrong. As for this page: last week's log named Palmer as a day-0 bet, the squad that took the field did not contain him, and Palmer then produced the highest midfield score of the opening weekend. The machine has a watchlist. It also had him.

plan.outlook: Gameweek 1 is finally complete, and it finished on Monday night at Craven Cottage rather than on Saturday afternoon. Le Professeur leads the five on 64 and is second in the league, six behind Gunners.exe; Mr CR7 is on 58, then Xabi on 50, Sir Fergie on 49 and The Special One on 44 — twenty points covering all five, which is one captain and one bench ordering. Three things actually happened. Chelsea's opener paid every squad in this league at once, because all five own João Pedro and three own Rogers, so it moved nobody relative to anybody. Both captaincy options returned two, so the armband separated nobody either. And the one Chelsea player who beat all of them, Palmer, is owned by none of the five — which, alongside Ødegaard, is now the room's shape rather than its bad luck. There is no transfer before Friday's deadline that would survive being written down: Palestra and Aït-Nouri are dead slots but cheap ones, the Hull defenders are all flagged, Sangaré and De Cuyper have one game each, and Gakpo and Watkins are both mid-transfer. The three real decisions are still later — the United block at Old Trafford in GW4, whether anyone fixes the Arsenal-midfield hole, and whether a second chip gets spent in August.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded — but Gameweek 1, with every squad fifteen fit players and no doubles anywhere, is neither. One of the five found that out for six points, and still leads, which is the more interesting half of the sentence.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.
